question: Which unsupervised methods (PCA, K-means, hierarchical, model-based clustering) extract structure from unlabeled data, and how must data be scaled for them?

results.claim: PCA of CVX and XOM returns gives a first component that is roughly an average of the two.
results.setup: Worked example in R on S&P 500 daily stock returns (sp500_px), book data; princomp on CVX, XOM
results.quote:
The weights for CVX and XOM for the first principal component are –0.747 and –
0.665

results.claim: K-means with 5 clusters on 16 stocks (nstart=10) gave balanced cluster sizes.
results.setup: Worked example in R on S&P 500 daily stock returns (sp500_px), book data from 2011-01-01; 16 symbols; kmeans centers=5, nstart=10

results.claim: Unscaled K-means on loan data gives one tiny cluster dominated by income and revolving balance.
results.setup: Loan defaults data (defaults), 6 numeric vars, kmeans centers=4 nstart=10, no scaling; cluster sizes 55, 1218, 7686, 14177
results.quote:
Cluster 1 has only 55 members with comparatively high
income and revolving credit balance.

results.claim: After z-score scaling the same K-means gives much more balanced cluster sizes.
results.setup: Same loan data, scale() then kmeans centers=4 nstart=10
results.quote: The cluster sizes are more balanced
results.note: Sizes read from the printed table; quote is the text statement.

results.claim: mclust on XOM/CVX returns picked 2 components with sizes 963 and 168, unlike compact K-means clusters.
results.setup: Worked example in R on S&P 500 daily stock returns (sp500_px), book data from 2011-01-01; Mclust(df), n=1131, BIC -4573.546
results.quote: Mclust VEE (ellipsoidal, equal shape and orientation) model with 2 components

results.claim: Single linkage assigns almost all points to one cluster; Ward's method is most similar to K-means.
results.setup: XOM/CVX returns, hclust with four dissimilarity measures, 4 clusters each (Fig 7-8)
results.quote:
the single linkage measure assigns almost all
of the points to a single cluster

results.claim: With GOOGL and AMZN added, the first two principal components are almost entirely those two stocks (loadings 0.781, 0.593 on PC1).
results.setup: PCA on 18 stocks from 2005-01-01 incl. GOOGL, AMZN, unscaled (princomp)
results.quote:
The first two principal components are almost completely dominated by GOOGL
and AMZN.

results.claim: K-means on z-scored dummy variables yields clusters that just proxy the factor levels.
results.setup: Loan data with dti, payment_inc_ratio, home (one-hot), pub_rec_zero; z-scored; kmeans centers=4
results.quote:
The top four clusters are essentially proxies for the different levels of the factor
variables.

results.claim: Hierarchical clustering does not scale well beyond modest sizes; K-means is the main method for very large data.
results.quote:
For even modest-
sized data with just tens of thousands of records, hierarchical clustering can
require intensive computing resources.

limits: All results are single worked examples on stock and loan data, with no timing, repeats or error bars.
Authors concede that for noisy data K-means, hierarchical and model-based clustering give very different solutions with no rule of thumb.
Model-based clustering depends on its distributional assumption and costs more compute than hierarchical clustering; the chapter covers only a small part of mclust.
Code is R (princomp, kmeans, hclust, mclust, daisy); formulas are images and are not in the text.
practices: Standardize (z-score) numeric variables before PCA and K-means, else large-scale variables dominate (Scaling the Variables).
For PCA, z-scores are equivalent to using the correlation matrix instead of the covariance matrix (princomp cor argument) (Scaling note).
Choose the number of principal components by screeplot, a cumulative-variance threshold such as 80%, loading interpretability, or cross-validation (How many components).
Run K-means with several random starts (nstart) and keep the lowest within-cluster SS (K-Means Algorithm).
Choose K from practical considerations first; use the elbow method (percent variance explained) or the gap statistic only as aids (Selecting the Number of Clusters).
Inspect cluster sizes and means; imbalanced clusters may signal outliers needing inspection (Interpreting the Clusters).
Check whether clusters would replicate on new data, e.g. by cross-validation (Selecting the Number of Clusters).
For mixed numeric and categorical data on smaller sets, use hierarchical clustering with Gower's distance rather than K-means or PCA (Problems with Clustering Mixed Data).
Scale one-hot binary variables to smaller variance, or cluster within subsets by category, for very large data (Problems with Clustering Mixed Data).
When one or two variables dominate PCA loadings, include them as is, rescale, or exclude and handle separately; no single correct approach (Dominant Variables).
Use clustering to start a cold-start problem and to identify subpopulations for separate models or as a feature (chapter intro).

terms.definition: A linear combination of the predictor variables.
The weights that transform the predictors into the components.
A plot of the variances of the components, showing the relative importance of the components.
The vector of variable means for the records in a cluster.
A visual representation of the records and the hierarchy of clusters to which they belong.
A measure of how close one cluster is to another.
A scaling algorithm applied to mixed numeric and categorical data to bring all variables to a 0-1 range.
The point where the cumulative variance explained flattens out after rising steeply.
Max, min and mean pairwise distance between clusters; minimum variance (Ward) minimizes within-cluster SS like K-means.
Selects the best-fitting model with a penalty for the number of parameters; mclust picks the number of clusters with largest BIC.
